en: The Thirteen-Book Collection of Birth Stories (Jātaka),
Chapter on Mangoes (Ambavagga)
6. The Kāliṅga-Bodhi Jātaka:
King Kāliṅga was a wheel-turning monarch who ruled the earth with righteousness.
Kāliṅga and Bhāradvāja came into the presence of the Bodhi tree by means of a nāga of great power.
Having surrounded King Kāliṅga, that outcaste ascetic,
as he was setting the wheel of sovereignty in motion,
spoke these words with palms joined in reverence.
“Descend, O Great King,
for this ground has been leveled by the ascetics;
here, the Buddhas dwell in peace.”
The Fully Awakened Ones shine forth.
On this portion of ground,
the grasses and creepers turn to the right.
"The essence [of the earth] is at the navel of the earth;
thus we have heard in the mantras, O Great King,
regarding this world bounded by the ocean."
To Medinī, the supporter of all beings,
to this Earth— the very essence—
having descended, pay homage.
Those who are Nāgas and those who are noble elephants—
by this much they have attained their station.
The noble elephants do not flee. O noble elephant,
send forth the tusker at your will.
"To this extent,
O Naga, it is possible for one to approach this region.
Having heard that, the King of Kalinga—
Having listened to the words of the fortune-teller,
he sent for the Naga, thinking:
"We shall find out what this man's speech means."
And when he had been dismissed by the king,
the elephant, having trumpeted like a crane,
turned back and sat down.
Like one unable to bear a heavy burden,
Kāliṅga Bhāradvāja,
having realized that the Nāga’s life-span was exhausted;
Hurrying toward King Kāliṅga, he addressed him:
“Mount another elephant, O Nāga!”
“O Great King, the elephant’s life-span is exhausted.
Having heard this, the King of Kalinga hurriedly approached the elephant.
As if the king had passed away,
the elephant fell right there upon the ground;
such was the word of the physiognomist.
In such a manner did the Naga speak.
King Kaliṅga said this to the Brāhmaṇa of Kaliṅga:
“You alone are the Fully Awakened One,
the All-Knowing, the All-Seeing.
Not tolerating this from Kāliṅga, [he said:]
The brahmin said this:
“For we are fortune-tellers,
O Great King, while the Buddhas are all-knowing.”
The All-Knowing and All-Seeing Buddhas do not know by means of characteristics;
for we rely on the power of the scriptures.
The Buddhas understand everything.
Having magnified full enlightenment while various musical instruments were being played;
Having brought garlands and ointments,
the king then departed with sixty thousand wagons.
The King of Kalinga gathered flowers and honored the unsurpassed seat of enlightenment.
The Kāliṅgabodhi Jātaka, the sixth.
